issues.failure_explanation: The data are sampled at H=mh, so a zero-loss solution must satisfy p(ξ)^m=e^{λmh}. The lemma instead asserts p(ξ)=e^{λh} for the minimizer. When m>1, other m-th roots are also global minimizers and can change the sign of the imaginary part. The Nyquist condition should therefore be imposed on λmh, not λh.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the one-step analysis to m=1, or explicitly impose p(ξ)=e^{λh} as a branch-selection condition and replace the Nyquist condition with one on λmh; then restate the dependent sign results for the selected branch.
issues.overall_effect: The one-step minimizer characterization and the phase-sign conclusions derived from it are unreliable for substepping with m>1 unless a branch is selected and the sampling Nyquist condition is corrected.
issues.title: One-step minimizer condition ignores m-th roots and sampling step H=mh
issues.why_classification: A supported repair is available by adding a branch/sampling restriction, but it excludes or weakens the advertised general m>1 regime and requires revisiting dependent sign claims.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated hypotheses do not require Re(λ)=0. For example, if λh=1/2, the Forward Euler exact-fit solution is ξ=e^{1/2}-1 with positive real part, contradicting Re(λ̂)<0. The proof uses the conservative identity Re(λh)=0. Also, for λ=0 the unique FE minimizer is ξ=0, so the strict inequality Re(λ̂)<0 fails.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By Theorem~\ref{thm:one-step-dissipative-theorem}, for dissipative systems, $\hat\lambda h$ is always confined in the stability region of the given method; i.e., $|p(\hat\lambda h)|<1.$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof invokes a complex “mean value theorem” on a line segment in a way that is not a valid scalar complex MVT, and the algebraic identity used is not justified. In addition, the lower bound |p(ηh)|^k|p'(ηh)|≥c0 for all k is incompatible with the dissipative case |p(ηh)|<1, since |p(ηh)|^k tends to zero as k grows. Thus the stated O(σ²) bound is not established.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows that the particular solution generated by the sampled exponential has |z_n|=1. Absolute stability, however, requires all characteristic roots to lie in the unit disc. A learned ξ can have unstable roots that are not excited by the chosen initial data, so |z_n(ξ)|=1 does not imply ξ is on the boundary of the absolute stability region.
